growth: Lab 10 base 3%; FY2025 operating revenue grew 12.77%, influenced by mix and pricing. 0–6% is an analyst scenario range.
One aggregate driver does not separate membership, pricing, premiums and Carelon.
Membership, premium yields, Medicaid rate adequacy and Carelon external revenue.
margin_shift: Shift all five base margins: 14.3, 14.5, 14.7, 14.8, 14.8%. FY2025 blended margin 14.2638%. Bounds are analyst stresses.
This is not medical benefit ratio: benefits and product costs are blended over total operating revenue.
Medical utilization, pricing, payer mix and Carelon product economics.
expense_shift: Efficiency gains may be offset by staffing, compliance or technology costs.
Reported operating expenses, identified noncash items and sustainable efficiency evidence.
claims_days: FY2025 ending claims / annual benefits ×365 =42.07; prior lab history 2024=45.05 and 2023=47.30. Bounds are stresses.
Ending balance is not an actuarial adequacy test; slower payment is not better underwriting.
Claims payment patterns, reserve development and statutory filings.
capex: FY2025 capex 1116; prior lab FY2024=1256, FY2023=1296. Bounds test underinvestment and higher technology spend.
Flat spending may understate replacement and growth requirements.
Capital commitments and software investment needed to support services growth.
tax: 24% judgment replaces FY2025 effective rate 15.63%; tax benefits are not assumed to repeat.
Cash taxes may differ from book tax; losses get no automatic tax asset.
Tax-note changes and a normalized cash-tax reconciliation.
investment_income: 2194 reported less 398 equity-method earnings =1796. Portfolio balances held flat.
Remainder is assumed cash; flat assets and income miss reinvestment, duration and growth.
Portfolio yields, reinvestment cash flows and upstream cash availability.
debt_rate: FY2025 interest / closing debt =4.375%; applied to opening forecast debt. Not a market quote.
Closing debt is not average debt; refinancing cost may differ.
Debt maturity, coupon and refinancing schedules.
repayment: Lab 10 judgment; assumes other maturities are refinanced and scheduled net paydown stops after 2030.
A perpetual no-paydown terminal is a classroom simplification.
Parent debt maturities, leverage targets and refinancing access.
buyback: Hold FY2025 repurchases at 2605; dividends fixed at 1529. Upper bound deliberately tests funding strain.
Payouts can exhaust liquidity; no execution-price/share-reduction schedule is modeled.
Parent liquidity, regulated dividends, repurchase plans and authorization.
ke: Lab 10 required-return judgment. 8–12% is a sensitivity interval, not an estimated confidence interval.
Insurer equity risk needs a dated capital-market calibration.
Risk-free yield, equity risk premium, beta and capital/underwriting risk.
terminal_growth: Lab 10 mature nominal growth judgment. All rates below the cost-of-equity bounds.
Extrapolation does not explicitly fund statutory capital growth or portfolio growth.
Long-run growth, required capital and subsidiary dividend capacity.
